description: Use this when the user asks to be told when a DNS change they are making has finished ("let me know when it's live"). Starts a free watch on ONE record for the signed-in user: DNS Doctor rechecks it every 10 minutes for up to 48 hours with the same verdict as check_record and sends ONE email to the address on their DNS Doctor account: when it is live, when the value has sat at a different name for an hour, when the zone has not served it for 6 hours, or when 48 hours pass. Same arguments as check_record; pass expected_value when the user is publishing a specific value. It reads the record once first and returns that reading: a record that is already live (verdict done), a domain whose nameservers do not answer, or a lookup fault starts nothing. Asking again for the same record returns the running watch, never a second one. Relay `watch.note`. Needs a linked DNS Doctor account; never ask the user for an email address. Nothing is applied to anyone's DNS.

domain.description: The domain to check, e.g. example.com. Bare registrable names and subdomains both work; scheme, path or port do not belong here. Unicode names are accepted and normalized to punycode.
domain.title: Domain

expected_value.description: Optional: the exact value just published (e.g. the DMARC record text, a verification token, '10 mx.example.com'). Given it, the verdict tests for that value and an 'edit' also checks the names a misplaced edit usually lands on (found_at).
expected_value.title: Expected Value

host.description: Optional label to prepend to the domain (e.g. 'mail' to check mail.<domain>) — honored for txt, cname, a and aaaa only; spf, dmarc and mx derive their own query name.
host.title: Host

kind.description: Which record to read; the right query is derived from it — 'dmarc' reads TXT at _dmarc.<domain> filtered to v=DMARC1, 'spf' reads the apex TXT filtered to v=spf1, so don't prefix the domain yourself.
kind.title: Kind
